thread.title: Broadcom (AVGO) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Broadcom (AVGO) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Shutterstock photo Broadcom ( AVGO ) is set to report third quarter fiscal 2018 earnings results after the closing bell Thursday.
The semiconductor giant, which also has a leading position in wired infrastructure and wireless communication markets, has seen its stock punished over the past three months, falling 14% year to date, including losing some 16% over the past month. This compares to the 7% rise in the S&P 500 index and the more than 12% rise in the iShares PHLX Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ).
Broadcom’s underperformance was driven by a combination of events, namely the company’s announcement to buy CA Inc. ( CA ) for $19 billion. This is a deal Wall Street hated. What’s more, in the second quarter, though the company beat on both the top and bottom lines, the management warned of slower sales in wireless, forecasting Q3 revenue to be in the range of $5.05 billion, plus or minus $75 million, while analysts expect net revenue of $5.23 billion.
To the extent the management on Thursday can sell investors on the benefits of the deal, while outlining improving business conditions, the stock could rebound strongly. Combined with a strong top- and bottom-line beat, Broadcom’s decline could be a thing of the past, especially with Apple’s ( AAPL ) new iPhones — to which it provides wireless components — due to be released.
For the quarter that ended July, Wall Street expects the the company to earn $4.82 per share on revenue of $5.07 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came came to $4.10 per share on revenue of $4.47 billion. For the full year, ending October, earnings are projected to rise 25% to $20 per share, while full-year revenue of $20.75 billion would mark a 17.5% increase year over year.
The year-over-year comps — on a percentage gain basis — would still be impressive, if achieved. But investors are still holding their collective breath, given the company’s own statements about what to expect on Thursday. Sales of chips to the datacenter segment, which has been a source of strength for Broadcom, is expected to remain strong and offsetting slowing smartphone sales.
But how much weakness should investors expect? Analysts have warned of slowing iPhone sales each quarter and Apple has done nothing but demolish those expectations on its way to $1T market cap. Broadcom’s relationship with Apple, to which it provides wireless components for the iPhones, could be a potential near-term catalyst as Apple is set to unveil its new iPhone lineup next week.
All told, with Broadcom stock down 22% from its all-time high, it seems the market has already priced in the lowered expectation. And given Broadcom’s strong track record of execution, buying low now looks like a sound strategy.
